candidates.tagline: Galway spent €28,000 on a 'g' that looks like a Belgian shopfitter
candidates.story: Galway City Council replaced its beloved 1984 capital 'G' logo with a generic lowercase 'g' for €28,000 — which the public immediately identified as nearly identical to a Belgian shopfitting company's brand — and councillors met today to vote on whether to scrap it.
candidates.why_funny: The city paid a branding agency €28,000 to produce something so generic it was already taken by a European shopfitter, while citizens erected 'Keep the G' protest flags around the city.
candidates.alt: Galway City Council's new brand identity displayed on a large outdoor hoarding, showing the new maroon lowercase 'g' logo on a maroon stripe alongside 'Comhairle Cathrach na Gaillimhe / Galway City Council' text and circular photos of Galway harbour and cathedral

candidates.tagline: Ferrari designed a car so sleek there was literally no room for windshield wipers
candidates.story: Ferrari's Jony Ive-designed Luce EV has a cowl so aerodynamically low there is no gutter for wiper blades, forcing Ferrari to file a patent for a new electromagnetic sliding wiper system — because they optimised the car's lines until rain became an engineering emergency.
candidates.why_funny: Ferrari spent years perfecting every curve of the Luce, then had to reinvent one of the oldest automotive components because nowhere on their beautiful car could traditional windshield wipers actually go.
candidates.alt: Baby blue Ferrari Luce EV photographed in three-quarter front view, showing the car's unusually low cowl and windshield wiper blades positioned vertically along the A-pillars rather than resting flat along the bottom of the windshield
